resources.string: AERIVA tells you what Android reports about your connection, in plain words. It has no account, and what it shows stays on this phone.
Reported by Android to AERIVA on %1$s.
Keep the latest changes in your connection on this phone for 30 days. Nothing is sent anywhere.
AERIVA shows what Android reports about your connection, in plain words. It does not measure your speed and it does not change your connection.

Android tests each network in the background to see whether it can reach the internet. A passed check means that test worked on that network. It does not guarantee that every app or website will load.

When more than one network is available, the one in use did not pass Android\'s check and another one did, Network Advisor suggests the other one. It only opens Android\'s own settings, and you decide whether to switch. It waits a short moment before speaking up, so a brief drop does not trigger it.

This list shows every network Android currently reports to AERIVA, with only the facts Android reports: whether its check passed, whether it is metered, and whether a sign-in page or a device policy was reported. Some phones keep mobile data off while Wi-Fi is connected, so you may see only one network.
AERIVA remembers the latest changes in your connection, only on this phone, and removes them after 30 days. You can turn this off or clear it in Settings.
AERIVA has no account and does not ask for the internet permission. Nothing it shows leaves your phone unless you choose to share a status report yourself.
